chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Wasil ibn Suleyman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

We mentioned the ring of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Would you like for me to show it to you?' So I said, 'Yes'. So he (peace be upon him) called for a sealed covering, opened it, and brought it out in a piece of cotton. Behold, it was a silver ring, and in it was a black stone, upon which were inscribed two lines: 'Muhammad, Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the stone of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was black.'
ai.seo_question: What was the appearance and inscription of the Prophet Muhammad's ring?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a detailed physical description of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) signet ring, specifically identifying the black stone (likely a ruby or agate) and the silver band inscribed with 'Muhammad, Messenger of Allah'. It serves as a primary textual basis for the Shia scholarly tradition regarding the authenticity of the Prophet's personal effects and the permissibility of using signet rings for sealing documents, reinforcing the practice of carrying one's name and prophetic title as a mark of authority.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of his companions, from Wasil Bin Suleyman, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘We mentioned the ring of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Would you love it if I<sup>asws</sup> were to show it to you?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> called for a sealed covering, so he<sup>asws</sup> opened it and brought out a cotton sheet, so there was a silver ring and in it was embedded a black stone, and upon it was inscribed in two lines – “Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup>”’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The stone of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was black’.
en.sarwar: 7. Sahf ibn Ziyad has narrated from certain persons of his people from Wasil ibn Sulayman from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Once we mentioned the ring of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and he (the Imam) said, ‘Will you like if I show you?’ I replied, ‘Yes, (I will be delighted to see it).’ He (the Imam) then asked for a sealed package and took from it a pack of cotton in which there was a ring of silver. It had a piece of black stone with two lines of writing that said, ‘Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.’ He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) said, ‘The stone of the ring of the Holy Prophet is black.’”
